CUSTOMER ANALYTICS · FICTIONAL CAFÉ

K-means for
café customers

Campus Café records each customer’s monthly spending and number of visits. Use k-means clustering to put customers with similar values into groups.
30 customers · 2 features · 1 month

PROCEDURE

Group the café customers

Each small mark = one customer✚ = centroid

The analyst selects the features. K-means uses them to form clusters.

Features can be single variables, combined scores, or PCA components that combine several variables.

K-means can use more than two dimensions. The selected features and their scales determine what “similar” means.

Feature scaling: The calculation divides spending by $200 and visits by 20. A $10 difference and a one-visit difference have equal weight. The axes show the original units.

Inertia —
K-means decreases the sum of squared distances.

Select the next step. To go directly to a stage, select its number.

Select a customer to compare the distances to all centroids.

Select a term to see its definition. You can also put the pointer on the term.
